themes_detail.label: Street Deterioration Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints have spiked to 141 THIS WEEK—a 271% increase over the 8-week average of 38 complaints per week—suggesting rapid deterioration across CD 405 that may require immediate DOT intervention.
evidence: 141 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 38.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.91)
271% spike is highest severity recorded in dataset
Long-standing CB budget request for sewer inspection and repair on specific street segments suggests chronic underinvestment
reporting_angles: Walk streets with residents and photograph worst problem areas; interview DOT about repair timeline
Analyze which streets are getting complaints; cross-reference with last pothole repair dates

themes_detail.label: Dead and Dying Trees Surge
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints jumped to 10 THIS WEEK—a 515% spike over the 8-week baseline of 1.6 per week—indicating possible storm damage, disease outbreak, or neglect in the district's canopy.
evidence: 10 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.6 weekly average (z-score: 7.54)
515% increase is second-highest severity in dataset
Recurring CB budget requests for park and amenity reconstruction suggest deferred maintenance culture
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department to identify cause: storm damage, disease, or systemic underfunding of tree care?
Interview Parks officials and arborists about remediation plans and replanting timeline

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Spike
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints spiked to 18 THIS WEEK—a 148% jump from the 8-week average of 7.2 per week—suggesting a potential pest outbreak or sanitation breakdown across the district.
evidence: 18 rodent complaints THIS WEEK vs. 7.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.6)
148% increase indicates emerging pattern, not baseline noise
Coincides with sanitation worker complaint spike (3 THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 avg, +500%), suggesting possible service disruption
reporting_angles: Interview DSNY about whether sanitation pickup has been disrupted or routes changed recently
Canvass affected blocks to identify common factors: construction, restaurant/food storage, waste management

themes_detail.label: Traffic Signal Failures Plateau
themes_detail.summary: Traffic signal condition complaints peaked 3 weeks ago at 221 (431% above baseline of 41.6 weekly average), but signal timing and data suggest an ongoing infrastructure crisis rather than acute incident.
evidence: Peak of 221 complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 41.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 6.72)
431% spike indicates major signal failure event or district-wide malfunction
No recent follow-up data provided; unclear if issue is resolved or still ongoing
reporting_angles: Verify current status: Are signals still malfunctioning or has DOT resolved the 3-week-ago crisis?
Interview DOT and local elected officials about response time and infrastructure investment

themes_detail.label: Building Code Violations Uptick
themes_detail.summary: Building/use complaints jumped to 22 THIS WEEK—a 132% increase from the 8-week average of 9.5—potentially signaling unsafe conditions or code enforcement gaps as 385 DOB permits remain in process.
evidence: 22 building/use complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.06)
132% spike during period of elevated DOB permit activity (385 filings in last 90 days, including 41 new buildings and 9 demolitions)
Recurring CB budget request for additional building inspectors suggests chronic enforcement staffing gap
reporting_angles: Interview DOB about inspector capacity: Are complaints rising because violations are increasing or because enforcement is lagging?
Cross-reference complaint locations with active construction permits to identify any pattern
